summary: The paper presents a design for user-defined data distributions as first-class objects in Chapel, built from domains, index sets, a global mapping from indices to locales and an optional locale-internal layout. It illustrates the design with cyclic and block classes and a sparse case, and states that the implementation is underway, with no performance results yet.
why_read: It shows how a high-level parallel language can let programmers write distribution policies as ordinary code while the compiler generates the local and remote accesses.
main_contribution: A user-defined distribution facility for Chapel, with formal definitions of global mapping and layout and a base-class interface for distribution writers.
main_limitation: The paper states that performance results are not yet available and that alignments, full halo specification and efficient dynamic distribution management are not covered.
